name: Spear-thrower
desc: The atlatl lengthened the thrower's arm, greatly increasing the range and force of thrown darts.

name: Sling
desc: A cord-and-pouch projectile weapon used from the Neolithic to Roman times.

name: Mace
desc: A club with a heavy stone or metal head, among the earliest weapons made specifically for combat.

name: Longbow
desc: A tall self bow, known from Ötzi's equipment and later decisive for English armies at Crécy and Agincourt.

name: Composite bow
desc: Bows laminated from wood, horn and sinew gave great power in a short length, ideal for mounted archers.

name: Dagger
desc: Short stabbing blades, first in flint and then copper and bronze, the ancestor of the sword.

name: Shield
desc: Hand-held barriers of wood, hide and later metal, used by nearly every ancient army.

name: Helmet
desc: Metal head protection appears in Sumer around 2500 BC, as in the helmet of Meskalamdug at Ur.

name: Scale armour
desc: Overlapping metal scales sewn to a backing, worn by charioteers in the Bronze Age Near East.

name: Lamellar armour
desc: Small plates laced together in rows, widely used from Assyria to East Asia and the steppe.

name: Mail
desc: Interlinked iron rings, probably invented by the Celts, gave flexible protection for nearly two thousand years.

name: Plate armour
desc: Full suits of shaped steel plates protected late medieval knights against swords and arrows.

name: War chariot
desc: Spoked-wheel horse chariots of the Sintashta culture became the elite striking arm of Bronze Age armies.

name: Bronze Age sword
desc: Lengthened bronze blades produced the first true swords in the Aegean and Near East.

name: Iron Age sword
desc: Swords of wrought iron and later steel replaced bronze as iron working spread.

name: Pike
desc: Very long infantry spears such as the Macedonian sarissa, revived by Swiss pikemen in the 15th century.

name: Pilum
desc: The Roman heavy javelin, whose soft iron shank bent on impact to disable enemy shields.

name: Defensive wall
desc: Walls around settlements, beginning with Neolithic Jericho, protected communities from attack.

name: Castle
desc: Fortified residences of medieval lords, evolving from timber mottes to stone keeps and concentric walls.

name: Bastion fort
desc: Low angled earth and masonry ramparts, the trace italienne, resisted cannon fire and covered approaches with flanking fire.

name: Battering ram
desc: Heavy beams for breaking gates and walls, depicted in Egyptian and Assyrian sieges.

name: Siege tower
desc: Wheeled towers let attackers reach the tops of walls, used by the Assyrians and later the Greeks and Romans.

name: Crossbow
desc: A bow mounted on a stock with a mechanical trigger, used on a large scale in Warring States China.

name: Gastraphetes
desc: A Greek belly-bow drawn using body weight, the forerunner of the catapult.

name: Catapult
desc: Engineers of Dionysius I of Syracuse built mechanical artillery to hurl bolts and stones at sieges.

name: Ballista
desc: Torsion-powered bolt and stone throwers using twisted sinew springs, standard in Hellenistic and Roman armies.

name: Traction trebuchet
desc: A Chinese lever-arm siege engine powered by crews pulling ropes, which spread west by the 6th century.

name: Counterweight trebuchet
desc: A falling counterweight powered this siege engine, able to hurl stones of over 100 kg against walls.

name: Trireme
desc: A Greek warship with three banks of oars, built to ram enemy vessels.

name: Naval ram
desc: A bronze-sheathed beak on a warship's bow used to hole enemy hulls.

name: Greek fire
desc: An incendiary liquid projected from siphons by the Byzantine navy, credited with defending Constantinople.

name: Fire arrow
desc: Arrows carrying gunpowder incendiaries, first recorded in Song-era China.

name: Fire lance
desc: A tube of gunpowder on a spear that fired flame and shrapnel, the ancestor of all guns.

name: Grenade
desc: Ceramic and iron shells filled with gunpowder thrown by hand, first used in Song China.

name: Land mine
desc: Buried explosive devices were first used by Song forces against the Mongols.

name: Hand cannon
desc: A metal-barrelled firearm, as in the Heilongjiang hand cannon of about 1288.

name: Cannon
desc: Large gunpowder tubes firing projectiles appeared in Europe by 1326, reshaping sieges.

name: Hwacha
desc: A Korean cart that launched dozens of rocket-propelled arrows at once.

name: Matchlock
desc: A lever lowering a burning match to the priming pan, the first trigger mechanism for firearms.

name: Arquebus
desc: A shoulder-fired matchlock gun that became the standard infantry firearm of the 16th century.

name: Mortar
desc: Short-barrelled guns firing at high angles, first used at the siege of Constantinople.

name: Rifling
desc: Spiral grooves in a barrel spin the bullet, greatly improving accuracy.

name: Wheellock
desc: A spring-driven steel wheel struck sparks from pyrite, allowing guns to be carried ready to fire.

name: Musket
desc: A heavier long gun able to pierce plate armour, used by massed infantry for three centuries.

name: Naval mine
desc: Floating explosive devices against ships were described in Ming China; Bushnell used them in 1777.

name: Flintlock
desc: Marin le Bourgeoys' flint-striking lock was cheaper and more reliable, standard until the 1840s.

name: Bayonet
desc: Blades fixed to musket muzzles let musketeers defend themselves and made the pike obsolete.

name: Ship of the line
desc: Large sailing warships carrying rows of broadside guns, built to fight in line of battle.

name: Howitzer
desc: Artillery firing explosive shells on curved trajectories, between a gun and a mortar.

name: Mysorean rockets
desc: Iron-cased rockets used by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan against the British East India Company.

name: Congreve rocket
desc: William Congreve's British military rockets were based on captured Mysorean designs.

name: Percussion cap
desc: A copper cap of shock-sensitive fulminate made ignition reliable in wet weather.

name: Dreyse needle gun
desc: The first military bolt-action breech-loading rifle, adopted by Prussia, which allowed firing while prone.

name: Revolver
desc: Samuel Colt's revolving-cylinder pistol, mass-produced from interchangeable parts.

name: Telescopic sight
desc: Telescopes mounted on rifles for precise aiming, used by sharpshooters from the 1830s.

name: Metallic cartridge
desc: Self-contained metal cases holding primer, powder and bullet made breech-loading practical.

name: Guncotton
desc: Christian Schönbein's nitrated cotton was the first high-energy propellant, later the basis of smokeless powder.

name: Minié ball
desc: A hollow-based bullet that expanded into rifling, making rifles as fast to load as muskets.

name: Armstrong gun
desc: William Armstrong's rifled breech-loading cannon introduced built-up steel construction.

name: Ironclad warship
desc: Steam warships protected by iron armour, beginning with the French Gloire, made wooden fleets obsolete.

name: Repeating rifle
desc: Magazine-fed rifles such as the Spencer and Henry let soldiers fire several shots without reloading.

name: Gatling gun
desc: Richard Gatling's hand-cranked multi-barrel gun delivered sustained rapid fire.

name: Torpedo
desc: Robert Whitehead's self-propelled underwater weapon was powered by compressed air.

name: Bolt-action rifle
desc: The Mauser Model 1871 established the bolt action used by most rifles through two world wars.

name: Smokeless powder
desc: Paul Vieille's Poudre B gave higher velocity without obscuring smoke, enabling small-calibre automatic weapons.

name: Maxim gun
desc: Hiram Maxim's recoil-operated gun was the first fully automatic machine gun.

name: Semi-automatic rifle
desc: Rifles that reload themselves for each trigger pull, beginning with Mannlicher's designs.

name: Semi-automatic pistol
desc: Self-loading pistols fed from a magazine, beginning with the Borchardt C-93.

name: Shaped charge
desc: Charles Munroe observed that a hollow in an explosive focuses its force, later used against armour.

name: Destroyer
desc: Fast warships built to counter torpedo boats, later escorts and fleet workhorses.

name: Canon de 75 modèle 1897
desc: The French 75 was the first field gun with a hydropneumatic recoil mechanism, enabling rapid fire.

name: Military submarine
desc: John Holland's petrol-electric submarine, bought by the US Navy in 1900, set the pattern for modern submarines.

name: Flamethrower
desc: Richard Fiedler's portable flamethrower was first used by German troops in 1915.

name: Armoured car
desc: Armoured motor vehicles carrying machine guns, the predecessors of the tank.

name: Light machine gun
desc: Portable automatic weapons such as the Madsen let infantry squads carry machine-gun fire.

name: Electronic warfare
desc: Radio jamming during the Russo-Japanese War began the contest over the electromagnetic spectrum.

name: Dreadnought
desc: HMS Dreadnought's all-big-gun armament and steam turbines rendered earlier battleships obsolete.

name: Bomber
desc: Aircraft designed to drop bombs, beginning with Sikorsky's Ilya Muromets.

name: Synchronization gear
desc: Mechanisms timing a machine gun to fire through a spinning propeller, which created the fighter.

name: Fighter aircraft
desc: The Fokker Eindecker and later fighters were built to destroy other aircraft.

name: Chemical warfare
desc: Large-scale chlorine gas attacks at Ypres in 1915 began modern chemical warfare, later banned by treaty.

name: Gas mask
desc: Respirators with chemical filters were rushed into service to protect troops against poison gas.

name: Combat helmet
desc: Steel helmets such as the Adrian and Brodie cut head wounds from shell fragments in the First World War.

name: Depth charge
desc: Explosive canisters fused to detonate at depth, the first effective anti-submarine weapon.

name: Tank
desc: British tracked armoured vehicles first went into action at the Somme in 1916.

name: Submachine gun
desc: Automatic weapons firing pistol cartridges, such as the MP 18, for close combat.

name: Aircraft carrier
desc: HMS Argus was the first ship with a full-length flight deck, later the core of naval power.

name: Norden bombsight
desc: A gyroscopically stabilized analogue computer for high-altitude bomb aiming.

name: Nerve agent
desc: Gerhard Schrader's discovery of tabun led to the most lethal class of chemical weapons.

name: Night-vision device
desc: Infrared image converters first used in the Second World War, later passive image intensifiers.

name: Multiple rocket launcher
desc: Truck-mounted salvo launchers such as the Soviet Katyusha saturated areas with rockets.

name: Proximity fuze
desc: A tiny radar in a shell detonated it near its target, greatly increasing anti-aircraft effectiveness.

name: Bazooka
desc: A shoulder-fired rocket launcher with a shaped-charge warhead that gave infantry anti-tank firepower.

name: Flak jacket
desc: Body armour of steel or nylon plates protected bomber crews against shell fragments.

name: Chaff
desc: Clouds of foil strips swamped enemy radar, first used in the 1943 raid on Hamburg.

name: Precision-guided munition
desc: The radio-guided German Fritz X sank the battleship Roma, the first guided bomb success.

name: Acoustic homing torpedo
desc: Torpedoes that steered toward a target's propeller noise, first used by Germany and the US.

name: Cruise missile
desc: The pulse-jet V-1 flying bomb was the first operational cruise missile.

name: Ballistic missile
desc: The German V-2 was the first long-range guided ballistic missile.

name: Assault rifle
desc: The StG 44 fired an intermediate cartridge with selective fire, the pattern of modern infantry rifles.

name: Messerschmitt Me 262
desc: The first operational jet fighter, considerably faster than piston-engined opponents.

name: Thermonuclear weapon
desc: The US Ivy Mike test used a fission primary to ignite fusion, yielding about 10 megatons.

name: Surface-to-air missile
desc: Radar-guided missiles such as Nike Ajax were deployed to shoot down bombers.

name: Nuclear submarine
desc: USS Nautilus, powered by a reactor, could stay submerged for weeks.

name: Air-to-air missile
desc: Guided missiles such as the infrared-homing Sidewinder became the main weapons of fighters.

name: Anti-tank guided missile
desc: Wire-guided missiles such as the French SS.10 let infantry destroy tanks at long range.

name: ICBM
desc: The Soviet R-7 was the first missile able to deliver a nuclear warhead between continents.

name: Submarine-launched ballistic missile
desc: The US Polaris missile was first fired from a submerged submarine in 1960.

name: Ballistic missile submarine
desc: USS George Washington began deterrent patrols in 1960, making nuclear forces survivable.

name: Anti-ballistic missile
desc: A Soviet V-1000 interceptor destroyed a ballistic missile warhead in 1961, beginning missile defence.

name: Laser-guided bomb
desc: Bombs homing on reflected laser light, such as Paveway, were used in Vietnam.

name: MIRV
desc: Missiles carrying several separately aimed warheads, first deployed on the US Minuteman III.

name: Kevlar body armour
desc: Soft vests of DuPont's Kevlar aramid fibre became standard police and military protection.

name: Stealth aircraft
desc: Aircraft shaped and coated to reduce radar returns, beginning with the F-117 Nighthawk.

name: Loitering munition
desc: Weapons that wait over a target area before striking, starting with the anti-radar IAI Harpy.

name: Unmanned combat aerial vehicle
desc: Armed remotely piloted aircraft, such as the Predator fitted with Hellfire missiles, entered combat in 2001.

name: Cyberwarfare
desc: State-linked attacks on Estonian networks in 2007 marked the emergence of cyberwarfare.

name: Stuxnet
desc: A computer worm that physically damaged Iranian uranium centrifuges, the first known cyberweapon of its kind.

name: Directed-energy weapon
desc: The US Navy's Laser Weapon System was deployed on USS Ponce in 2014.

name: Hypersonic glide vehicle
desc: Manoeuvring warheads gliding at hypersonic speed, such as Russia's Avangard, entered service in 2019.

name: Boomerang
desc: Curved throwing sticks used for hunting and fighting, the oldest found in Poland and Australia.

name: Battle axe
desc: Axes designed for combat, made of stone and later bronze and iron, used across Eurasia.

name: Lorica segmentata
desc: Roman legionary armour of articulated iron strips, an early form of segmented plate.

name: Japanese sword
desc: Curved differentially hardened steel blades developed in Heian Japan.

name: Halberd
desc: A pole weapon combining axe blade, spike and hook, used by late medieval infantry.

name: Caltrop
desc: Spiked devices scattered on the ground to lame horses and slow infantry.

name: Repeating crossbow
desc: Chinese crossbows with a magazine and lever that allowed rapid successive shots.

name: Onager
desc: A late Roman single-armed torsion engine that lobbed stones in an arc.

name: Bombard
desc: Very large siege cannons that broke medieval walls, such as at Constantinople in 1453.

name: Pistol
desc: Small one-handed firearms made practical by the wheellock, adopted by cavalry.

name: Shrapnel shell
desc: Henry Shrapnel's timed shell burst in the air to scatter balls over troops.

name: Gun turret
desc: Rotating armoured gun mounts, used on USS Monitor, let warships aim without turning.

name: Napalm
desc: Gelled petroleum incendiary developed at Harvard, used in firebombing and later wars.

name: Motte-and-bailey castle
desc: Earthwork mounds topped by timber keeps, spread across Europe by the Normans.

name: Machine gun
desc: Fully automatic guns firing continuously while the trigger is held dominated the battlefields of the First World War.

name: Anti-aircraft gun
desc: High-angle guns were adapted to shoot at aircraft from the First World War onward.

name: Main battle tank
desc: Tanks combining heavy armour, firepower and mobility, such as the Centurion, replaced specialized types.

name: Reactive armour
desc: Explosive armour tiles disrupt incoming shaped-charge jets, first fielded by Israel in 1982.
